lead: Modern cars contain many small computers. They must share switch states, sensor readings and commands over short wires that survive electrical noise. CAN, the Controller Area Network, is a robust multi-master differential bus for that job. LIN, the Local Interconnect Network, is a cheaper single-wire master-slave sub-bus for windows, mirrors and seats. Their wires, frames, arbitration, error checks and timing decide whether a message arrives in time. A common exam calculation finds a CAN frame time from its bit count and bit rate.
prereq: You need: Unit 3 timers and interrupts; 4.2 SPI and I2C buses for master-slave bus ideas.

blocks.text: CAN means Controller Area Network. It is a multi-master serial bus for vehicles. Two twisted wires, CAN<sub>H</sub> and CAN<sub>L</sub>, carry one differential signal. A logic 0 is dominant: the driver pulls the two wires apart. A logic 1 is recessive: the driver releases the bus and a resistor returns the wires together. Dominant always overwrites recessive. The bus needs 120 Ω termination at both ends to absorb reflections. Classic CAN runs at up to 1 Mbit/s; automotive networks commonly use 125 kbit/s, 250 kbit/s, 500 kbit/s or 1 Mbit/s. A node can join or leave without stopping traffic.

A classic CAN data frame has these fields in order: SOF, ID, RTR, IDE, r0, DLC, Data, CRC, ACK, EOF, IFS. SOF is one dominant start bit. ID is the 11-bit standard identifier. The extended format uses a 29-bit ID. RTR marks a data frame or a remote request. IDE selects standard or extended format. r0 is reserved. DLC gives the data length in bytes, 0 to 8. Data is 0 to 8 bytes. CRC checks the frame. ACK is driven by every receiver that saw a good CRC. EOF marks the end. IFS separates frames. CAN FD keeps the same idea but allows up to 64 data bytes.

CAN uses CSMA/CD with bit-wise arbitration (some books call it CSMA/CA). A collision is detected bit by bit and the losing node stops without destroying the frame. A node waits for idle, then sends SOF. All nodes that want the bus send their ID at the same time. A 0 dominates a 1. A node that sends 1 and reads 0 loses arbitration and stops. The frame with the lowest numerical ID wins, because its early 0 bits beat the 1 bits of others. The ID is a priority label, not a destination address. Many nodes may consume the same frame.

blocks.where: T_frame is the frame time in seconds; N_bits is the total frame bits; R_bit is the bit rate in bit/s.

blocks.text: Bit stuffing inserts one opposite bit after five equal bits in SOF to CRC. The receiver removes it. A bit error, stuff error, CRC error, form error or ACK error makes a node send an error frame. Error frames destroy the bad frame so all nodes reject it. A transmitter repeats the frame. A receiver that has a good CRC drives ACK dominant. If no node drives ACK, the transmitter sees an ACK error.

Classic CAN carries at most 8 data bytes. CAN FD carries up to 64 data bytes and can switch to a faster data phase. The arbitration phase stays compatible. At 500 kbit/s one bit lasts 2 µs. At 1 Mbit/s one bit lasts 1 µs. The frame time is the bit count divided by the bit rate.

LIN means Local Interconnect Network. It is a cheap single-wire bus that runs at the 12 V battery level. It uses one master and up to 15 slaves. The data rate is up to 20 kbit/s. LIN is not multi-master. The master controls all traffic with a schedule table. The table lists which frame is sent in which time slot. The schedule table gives predictable latency. The sync byte lets each slave measure the bit time, so slaves need no crystal.

A LIN frame has a break, sync, ID, data and checksum. The break is a long low pulse (at least 13 bit times) that marks the start of a new frame. A sleeping node is woken by a separate wake-up pulse, not by the break. Sync is the byte 0x55, used to measure the bit time. ID is a 6-bit identifier plus two parity bits. Data is 1 to 8 bytes. Checksum covers the data and sometimes the ID. Slaves answer only when the master sends their ID. LIN is used for windows, mirrors, seats, wipers and other body functions. CAN links the major controllers; LIN links small body loads under one master.

examples.question: A classic CAN standard data frame carries 8 data bytes at 500 kbit/s. Its fields plus intermission total 111 bits before bit stuffing. Find the frame time and the maximum frame rate. Ignore stuffing bits.
steps: Maximum frame rate f = 1 / T = 1 / 0.000222 s ≈ 4504.5 frame/s.
Round to whole frames: about 4505 frame/s.
examples.answer: The frame time is 222 µs, so the maximum frame rate is about 4505 frames per second.
examples.check:
N_bits = 111
R_bit = 500_000
T_frame = N_bits / R_bit
f_frame = 1 / T_frame
print(T_frame)
print(round(f_frame))

traps: A CAN ID is a priority label, not a destination address. A node may send a frame that many nodes receive.
Lower numerical ID wins arbitration. This feels backwards because 0 is dominant. A node sending a larger ID loses.
LIN is single-wire master-slave, not multi-master. Only the LIN master starts frames; slaves answer on request.
Terminate CAN with 120 Ω at the two physical ends, not at every node.
Classic CAN data is 0 to 8 bytes; CAN FD is up to 64. Do not use 64 bytes for classic.

quiz.q: What do CAN and LIN stand for?
quiz.a: CAN is Controller Area Network; LIN is Local Interconnect Network.

quiz.q: State the LIN topology and maximum data rate.
Why does a lower CAN identifier win arbitration?
quiz.a: During arbitration each node sends its ID. A dominant 0 beats a recessive 1. The lower ID has an earlier 0 where a higher ID has 1, so the higher-ID node loses and stops.

quiz.q: A classic CAN frame has 111 bits at 250 kbit/s. Find its frame time.
List the fields of a classic CAN data frame in order.
quiz.a: SOF, ID, RTR, IDE, r0, DLC, Data, CRC, ACK, EOF, IFS.

quiz.q: Why is a CAN identifier not a destination address?
quiz.a: It names the message content and priority; many nodes can filter and receive it. Destination addressing would need more bits and would not give priority arbitration.

quiz.q: Choose CAN or LIN for a seat motor and for a powertrain sensor. Give one reason each.
quiz.a: Seat motor: LIN, because it is cheap single-wire and low speed. Powertrain sensor: CAN, because it is differential, robust and multi-master with priority.

beyond: Not for the exam. CAN FD is common in newer vehicles because it carries more data while keeping arbitration compatible. LIN 2.x adds improved checksum and diagnostics. Automotive Ethernet is now used for camera and radar data, with CAN and LIN still handling control. Search for CAN FD, LIN schedule table, and automotive Ethernet.
